walkthrough:
Equate the two functions to find their intersection points:
$$\frac{x}{2} - 2 = 4 + x - \frac{x^2}{2}$$

Multiply by $2$ and rearrange into standard quadratic form:
$$x - 4 = 8 + 2x - x^2 \implies x^2 - x - 12 = 0$$

Factorise and solve for the $x$-coordinates:
$$(x - 4)(x + 3) = 0 \implies x = 4 \quad \text{or} \quad x = -3$$

Find the corresponding $y$-coordinates using $y = \frac{x}{2} - 2$:
$$\text{For } x = 4: \quad y = \frac{4}{2} - 2 = 0 \implies (4, 0)$$
$$\text{For } x = -3: \quad y = \frac{-3}{2} - 2 = -3.5 \implies (-3, -3.5)$$
$$\text{Points of intersection: } (4, 0) \quad \text{and} \quad (-3, -3.5)$$

Set up the inequality $f(x) > g(x)$:
$$\frac{x}{2} - 2 > 4 + x - \frac{x^2}{2} \implies x^2 - x - 12 > 0$$

State the outside solution intervals:
$$x < -3 \quad \text{or} \quad x > 4$$

Form the composite function $fg(x) = f(g(x))$:
$$fg(x) = \frac{4 + x - \frac{x^2}{2}}{2} - 2 = 2 + \frac{x}{2} - \frac{x^2}{4} - 2 = \frac{x}{2} - \frac{x^2}{4}$$

Complete the square to find the maximum value:
$$fg(x) = -\frac{1}{4}(x^2 - 2x) = -\frac{1}{4}\left[(x - 1)^2 - 1\right] = \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{4}(x - 1)^2$$

State the range of $fg$:
$$\text{Range of } fg: \quad fg(x) \le \frac{1}{4} \quad \left(\text{or } \left(-\infty, \frac{1}{4}\right]\right)$$

For $x \ge k$ to be one-to-one, smallest $k = 1$.
walkthrough:
Find the turning point of the quadratic function $h(x) = 4 + x - \frac{x^2}{2}$:
$$h'(x) = 1 - x = 0 \implies x = 1$$

For $h(x)$ to have an inverse, it must be strictly decreasing and one-to-one on the domain $x \ge k$.
This requires the domain to be restricted to the right of the maximum turning point:
$$\text{Smallest value of } k = 1$$
